newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes lower late, sours helped by Cano.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes lower late, sours helped by Cano.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were lower across the board late Thursday as the broad market sell-off continued, though sour grades pulled back from their worst levels on news that production was shut-in at Occidental Petroleum Corp's 200,000 barrels per day Cano Limon field after a rebel bomb.
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) was down around 15 cents on the day at about $19.15/20 a barrel, compared with a low around $19.10.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded down at $1.35 under WTI Thursday mid-morning, matching Wednesday's lowest level. It traded up to $1.31 and was at $1.32/$1.26 late, brokers said.
"There was the Cano news and there was also some short covering going on," said a trader at an independent refiner.
Eugene Island followed WTS lower and was at $1.55/$1.50 under WTI before heading back to $1.45/$1.42 late. It traded at $1.46 and $1.45 below, traders said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James (LLS) was showing signs of easing after its recent rise, trading at 24 cents above WTI early then down to a low of 20 over, quoted late at 20/22.
A sale of a 550,000 barrel Colombian Cusiana cargo for mid-August delivery helped to ease LLS, which had been climbing because of a lack of expensive North Sea Brent in the Gulf of Mexico.
(Key CRU/TU and hit F9 for Foreign Crude Report).
WTI/Midland traded a range between 27 and 29 cents under WTI, little changed on the differential.
